With Comcept's and Star Citizen recent blunders, do you still have confidence in Kickstarter? Do ideas and concepts backed by industry professionals deserve hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars? If you backed Yuka Laylee or Bloodstained would consider ever backing another game if you were to be dissatisfied with the final product?

I've had pretty good luck with Kickstarter, if you define good luck as "Most of my projects eventually showed up". Quality has been sporadic though. I feel like Planetary Annihilation finally got good with their most recent Galactic War update. I mostly back boardgames though, and sadly there is no patching those. Got more than my fair share of absolute duds.

Actually the only two projects I backed which near as I can tell have completely failed are two documentaries. One about Go and another about D&D. The D&D one is especially bizarre since it seems like half the team split and wanted to do their own D&D documentary, resulting in them both fighting over raw materials the Kickstarter drive funded.

The problem is backers not understanding what Kickstarter is. And also what Early Access really means.

The easiest way to explain Kickstarter is basically throwing money out the window in hopes that something good will maybe come out of it. The pledge goal thing on Kickstarter decreases the barrier to be an early backer and risk your money going towards a project that gets canceled due to a lack of donations.

Early Access on the other hand is just a silly term to mean "release". If you buy something, buy it on its own merits, not on promises. For example, Prison Architect has been a functional and very fun game for the whole time it was in Early Access.

There are plenty of examples of successes and failures of both. Kickstarter is all about trust with whoever is making it. Early Access isn't that necessarily.

I wish I could upvoat you, because it's what you said plus gamers (and young/new devs) not understanding just how crazy time consuming creating games is. Even those who speak programer fluently can tell you the best of them can unknowingly create bugs that can slow the process down for not just days, but months.

This tied with transparency. Devs who don't know how to explain their process and updating to their audience risk losing trust regardless of their original good intentions.

/edited because I just gained the power to upvoat some more.

I never had much confidence in KS to begin with. You're basically give over your cash based on faith with the only thing back being the game in whatever state it ends up being in if at all. But it's still a great platform for developers that want to produce niche titles that the gaming industry has shown they won't fund. The only game I've given significant funds to is Camelot Unchained. And that was because it had been shown over a decade that no one was interesting in another MMO built upon RvR. And while I'll be upset if it ends up being a disappointment, I'm not going to blame it on KS. I knew the risk going in. Heck, just being that type of game, there WILL be people upset no matter how it ends up.

Well, this is ofc gaming sub, but kickstarter is not only for gaming. I bet music stuff, for example, happens more often.

But gaming? Yea, I'd still say it's successful. It's investing, not buying.

I spent a good chunk of my high school gaming years around Quake 2 mods eventually moving on to Half-life mods and Source mods. I've always loved being involved with an unfinished product. Hopped on just about every Beta I could get my hands on. All the early access stuff is really cool to me, I'm very comfortable with a non-finished product and waiting patiently to see where it goes. Sometimes it turns out amazing, sometimes it fizzles out and it was just a fun ride.

That being said I've not really been burned yet by Kickstarter. I tend not to back the big guys, but I've definitely thrown money at something that had already breached a million bucks. I dunno so far I still think it's a cool and exciting way to interact with the medium I love. As long as you know that you might as well be throwing your money down the toilet for all the garuntee you have about getting it back.

If Yuka Laylee doesn't turn out great, I'll be disappointed but not upset. I feel like I got to inject myself into the history of Rare just a tiny little bit. I've spent years saying "oh man I wish old Rare was still around" and now I have a chance to put my money where my mouth is. I can't be too upset at however that turns out.
I don't have any faith in preorders anymore, kickstarter or otherwise. Aside from Minecraft I've been satisfied with about 0 of them.

I'm unaware of any blunders with might no 9, can someone fill me in? I've noticed a lot of hate around Facebook groups toward comcept that I'm not understanding. I hear there were some PR issues, but people are calling the game a failure and they haven't played it. I'm a backer myself and have played the beta, seems like a solid megaman game to me. I stress that it's seemed more classic megaman style than x style. It was also a beta and not a finished product, some I'm not understanding the hatred toward the product.

I do not trust kickstarting games despite some great games coming from the platform. Hell, I don't trust Early Access despite that actually having something I can download and play when I buy in. Too many greedy people out there looking to capitalize on empty promises, or nostalgia.
If Yooka-Laylee sucks, there won't be any more games to back, because I'm killing everyone.
